Recommended protocol: cache each user’s hit indicator for all nine variant/checkpoint combinations, keeping pinned users and candidates unchanged. Bootstrap 200 users with replacement independently within each dataset; reuse identical resampled indices across models/checkpoints to preserve pairing, then average the four dataset means equally. Use 10,000 CPU-only replicates to report paired macro-HR@10 differences, 95% percentile intervals, and per-dataset differences. This applies [paired bootstrap principles](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html). Intervals describe user uncertainty conditional on these four datasets, fixed candidates and trained models; they exclude training-seed and candidate-sampling variability. Sampled HR@10 cannot establish full-catalog ranking improvements ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).

Disclose all nine scores, selection/tie-breaking rules, and any earlier adaptive searches. Selecting the maximum creates optimism; a nominal interval around the selected winner is not selection-adjusted ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Recommended diagnostics: repeat selection inside each bootstrap to report selection frequencies and score-gap stability, explicitly without claiming unbiased performance. For confirmatory comparisons, predefine the comparison family and use simultaneous bootstrap intervals or multiplicity-adjusted tests. Preserve the untouched host test for final assessment; bootstrap diagnostics require no retraining.

Equal-GPU-time comparisons should use identical hardware and explicit timing boundaries. Report total charged GPU-seconds, training/evaluation/diagnostic overhead, and actual optimizer updates, examples processed, effective epochs, batch size/accumulation, and seconds/update per dataset at each checkpoint. Plot HR@10 against elapsed time and updates using cached evaluations. Time measures practical efficiency; updates/epochs reveal whether gains accompany more optimization or greater per-update effectiveness, without proving causality. Count failed trials and search overhead within 43,200 GPU-seconds; report final inference separately. This follows [AlgoPerf’s emphasis on time-to-result](https://mlcommons.org/benchmarks/algorithms/).
